title: Nintendo Direct September 2026: Start Time, How To Watch, And What To Expect
description: With yesterday's Legend of Zelda Direct in the bag, it's time to take a broader look at what's coming to Switch consoles with the September Nintendo Direct. Yesterday's broadcast was mostly focused on the upcoming remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, but today, we're expecting to see a whole lot more than just the hero in green. In case you can't make it, we'll be covering each new announcement and trailer as they drop, so keep on scrolling to see all the reveals and hit your F5 key to refresh your feed as we dive into what should be a massive Nintendo Direct presentation. How to watch the September Nintendo Direct Once again, you can watch the presentation through Nintendo's official YouTube and Twitch channels. YouTube Twitch Nintendo Direct start time Hope you're in the mood to start your day bright and early, as the broadcast starts at 7 AM PT / 10 AM ET on September 9. Nintendo says the show will run for roughly 45 minutes, and it'll be followed by a Nintendo Treehouse livestream that'll feature gameplay from select titles. 7 AM PT 10 AM ET 3 PM BST 4 PM CEST 11 PM JST What to expect That's the big question, isn't it? As you'd expect, Nintendo is keeping quiet ahead of the Direct, but we're expecting the usual first-party games, upcoming titles from third-party partners, and related news. According to leakers, we could be in for a bumper reveal of Switch exclusives, as they're teasing a new Super Smash Bros. fighting game, a brand-new Star Fox, and a new 3D Mario to end the broadcast with a bang. Nintendo may need to pull a few heavy hitters out, considering that the Switch 2 price increased by $50 earlier this month, and having a stacked selection of upcoming games could be just what the company needs to start shifting units. Could we also get a new look at Pokemon Winds and Waves? Pokemon continues to be one of the biggest franchises on Nintendo hardware, and we wouldn't say no to a quick look at the game's region or even a few new pocket monsters.

title: Xbox Game Pass Adds A Great Call Of Duty Game Today
description: Xbox Game Pass grows today with the addition of a popular Call of Duty game. New to the service from today, September 8, is 2020's Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War. It's available on Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, and PC Game Pass, and the game supports cloud streaming as well. Developed by Treyarch and Raven, Black Ops Cold War is set in Cold War-era 1981, with its campaign following Russell Adler as he and his team seek out a spy named Perseus. The game also has multiplayer, of course, along with Zombies. Black Ops Cold War was a bit hit, becoming 2020's best-selling game overall in the US. Game Pass isn't done adding more titles this month, as The Royal Writ and Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O World Stage arrive on September 10, followed by RuneScape: Dragonwilds on September 15. After Microsoft bought Activision Blizzard, many assumed that back-catalog Call of Duty games would flood Game Pass, but that didn't happen. Instead of releasing Call of Duty games en masse to Game Pass, Microsoft has taken more of a selective approach. Black Ops Cold War is now just the sixth Call of Duty game on Game Pass, joining Call of Duty: WWII, Call of Duty: Vanguard, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, and Black Ops 6. Modern Warfare 3 and Black Ops 6 were released day-and-date into Game Pass, but that's ending this year, and any Game Pass subscriber who wants to play Modern Warfare 4 at launch this October will have to pay for it... or wait a year.

title: Why Is Link The Worst-Looking Character In The Ocarina Of Time Remake?
description: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake was always going to prove divisive. Whether it strove to be a faithful retelling or a bold reimagining like Final Fantasy 7 Remake, Zelda’s 3D debut is so beloved, so seminal, and so ingrained in our collective nostalgia that aiming to please everyone was always going to be impossible. Personally? I think it looks just fine. I was slightly underwhelmed by the fact that, aside from quality-of-life improvements and an essential modernization of certain gameplay mechanics, Nintendo is pretty much poised to deliver a 1:1 remake. The scale of characters, depth of locations, and overall scope of Link’s world is seemingly identical to the Nintendo 64 original. Monsters might be newly positioned and items could be gained in different ways, but it’s clear that the gameplay experience fans are intimately familiar with is being preserved. For better or worse. Putting gameplay improvements aside though, we need to talk about the visuals. I can’t lie; I got a little emotional when the gameplay demo dropped us straight into a modern take on Kakariko Village, demonstrating the remake’s take on Link glancing around at familiar houses, shops, and friends of the forest he has spent years growing up with. It’s just a shame that our Hero of Time doesn’t look like he belongs in this world at all thanks to his cumbersome design. There is no denying that Young Link is cute, yet he also feels strangely overdesigned as a way to flaunt both the best and worst parts of this new artistic direction. Link’s piercing blue eyes, rounded cheeks, and emotionless demeanor make him look weirdly out of place, like one of the creepy puppets from Jim Henson’s Labyrinth. This lack of expression worked in the Nintendo 64 original because of the technical limitations at the time, but future versions of Link from Wind Waker, Twilight Princess, and Breath of the Wild understood that even if our hero doesn’t speak, he still needs to act like a human being … or…

title: The Internet Reacts To Zelda: Ocarina Of Time’s Changes
description: Following the reveal of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's remake earlier this year, Nintendo shared an extended look at the game during the company's latest Direct. Naturally, players have been sharing their opinions on social media, and certain aspects of the game's art style has been divisive among the fan base. However, there have been some very positive reactions as well. The new looks for young Link and some of the other character inspired a round of memes and jokes. Some players had conflicted feelings about the remake's enhancements. And then there are the Zelda faithful who are thrilled to have Link and company back in an upgraded version of the classic game. At least one player was impressed by the game's new feature, which allows fans to hum one of the Zelda themes to make Link play it with his ocarina. The Direct also disclosed additional details about the remake, including Link's newfound ability to jump, the voice acting, and a game mechanic that was apparently borrowed from Breath of the Wild. Nintendo will release its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 on November 5. There will also be a Zelda concert tour in 2027.

title: Is The Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Even Bothering With Its Big Twist?
description: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 looks to be a faithful remake in a lot of ways, with some light modernization touches here and there. The story as we've seen it also looks very faithful, from the Great Deku Tree to the fearsome appearance of Ganondorf. But among the quick flashes of story sequences one character in particular caught my eye, and it made me wonder if this remake will be more overt with one of the series' most famous twists. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time spoilers follow. Ocarina of Time has a significant time jump, from child Link to adult Link, which earned this version of Link the nickname The Hero of Time. The child Link last saw Princess Zelda being spirited away from the castle by her bodyguard, Impa, during an apparent power grab by the evil Ganondorf. When Link takes the Master Sword and awakens as an adult, the castle is in disrepair, and the royal family is nowhere to be found. What exactly happened to Zelda is a major driving mystery through this second major act of the game. As those who have played Ocarina before know, adult Zelda is hiding in plain sight as the mysterious Sheik. Sheik presents themselves as a survivor of the Sheikah people and helps Link along his journey, pointing him in the right direction of the Seven Sages. Eventually Zelda reveals herself. It's a plot twist that seems obvious in hindsight. The golden-haired Sheik was always hidden behind scarves and had a vested interest in helping Link, but the character is male-presenting, and this was a game that frequently introduced new bespoke characters. Sheik was just another part of the network of people who helped Link along his journey, no different than his childhood friend Saria or the Zora princess Ruto. Not to mention, we hadn't seen adult Zelda at all until Sheik's big reveal, so there was no way to compare them. The dual-identity was, at least to a much younger me, legitimately surprising. That's not necessarily the case anymore. Zelda's dual…

title: We Need To See How Messed Up Majora’s Mask’s Moon Will Be In Ocarina of Time’s New Art Style
description: There's no denying that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake looks weird. Whether you think it skews too far into the direction of realism or you're bawling your eyes out over how good Hyrule looks all these decades later, it's strange to see such a distinct and recognizable game look like this. And I'm hoping that it's received well, because I would love to see the same treatment applied to Ocarina of Time's incredibly strange and dark sequel, The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask, if only too see just how messed up that moon is going to look. It's possible you've never played Majora's Mask but will immediately recognize one of its primary antagonists: a menacing and ever-present moon that is slowly hurtling towards Clock Town over the span of three days. As time progresses, its creepy grin edges closer and closer to the ground, a constant reminder of the impending doom that only you can stop. It's a striking design that, alongside the equally iconic design of the titular Majora's Mask, gives such a different look and feel to the majesty of Hyrule in Ocarina of Time. While the Nintendo 3DS remake offered a way to see this menancing moon in more detail, I really can't wait to see what Nintendo can do if it decides to go down the same route as its most recent remake. Based on the footage in the latest Nintendo Direct, faces seem to be a divisive topic when it comes to talking about the look of Ocarina of Time. Young Link has an incredible amount of detail to the point of uncanniness, and that extends to an arresting first look at young Zelda that stood out (to me at least) as the strangest interpretation of the lot. There are many others that look a lot better--adult Link and Sheik look pretty great--but these are all characters that were designed to be friendly and inviting. Majora's Mask, by contrast, has characters designed to look the exact opposite, meaning we could probably see some truly alarming recreations that would fit perfectly with the tone of the…

title: Check Out Call Of Duty’s Doom Skins In Black Ops 7 And Warzone
description: The final season of Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 arrives on September 17, and Activision has revealed a Doom crossover event and shop bundle. Players can earn free rewards themed around the franchise, and there are also several paid cosmetics as well. All of these new Call of Duty Doom skins are highlighted below. Doom event pass Starting on September 24, Call of Duty Season 6 will introduce a limited-time Doom event. This gives players the opportunity to earn cosmetics themed around the Doom franchise in both free and paid event tracks. While both tracks offer Doom items, the iconic Doom Slayer operator skin and his "Doom Guy" variant skin are locked behind the paywall. A price wasn't provided with the announcement, but Call of Duty’s event passes are typically $10. Doom villians shop bundle Additionally, there will be a shop bundle for fans who want to collect even more Doom-themed operator skins. The Tracer Pack: Doom Demonic Essence focuses on the villains of the franchise, and they are paired with a trio of weapon blueprints, a finishing move, and other cosmetic items. The full pack includes the following items: “Marauder” Jurado Operator Skin (Guild) “Icon of Sin” Samuels Operator Skin (JSOC) “Hellish Argent” M15 Mod 0 Assault Rifle (Tracers, Death FX) “Putrid Essence” Dravec 45 SMG (Tracers, Death FX) “Marauder’s Axe” Mace Melee Weapon Blueprint “Futile” Finishing Move “Prepared to Destroy” Emote “Cacodemon” Weapon Charm “Death Wave” Animated Emblem “Hell Invasion” Animated Calling Card “OG Icon” Sticker Season 6 brings Halloween to Black Ops 7 and Warzone with Call of Duty's annual The Haunting event. This update adds a new battle pass, more guns, Zombies maps, and a spooky variant of Warzone's Haven's Hollow. Season 6 and The Haunting will wrap up content for Black Ops 7, as Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 arrives on October 23.

title: Xbox’s Disc-To-Digital Program Has A Big Problem: Several Major Publishers Aren’t Participating
description: Xbox's disc-to-digital program looks like it could be a vital step forward for players who want to hold on to their physical games in an increasingly digital world, but it does have limits. Not every game publisher is on board with it, it seems, as Xbox users are reporting that four of the biggest companies aren't "participating" at all. So far, it looks like games from Sega, Square Enix, Ubisoft, and Bandai Namco are largely incompatible with the disc-to-digital service. As verified by Kotaku, popping in a disc for a game from one of those publishers could result in a "not participating in digital licensing" message. A fan effort to catalogue all the games that do work with it also shows which titles from those publishers are incompatible with disc-to-digital, so if you were holding on to a physical edition of Far Cry 4, Final Fantasy 15, or Dark Souls 3, you're out of luck. This could be rectified in the future if those publishers decide to sign up--Xbox has mentioned that this will be a gradual rollout for the service--but the current wording of the message and the sheer number of games involved suggest otherwise. What's the reason for this? It could be down to good ol' economics, as the companies would probably prefer that you buy one of their games again on the digital storefront. After all, if you decide to pick up a physical copy of a title from a local secondhand store or through a private sale, they're not seeing a cent of that cash when it changes hands. This is something that Square Enix has been called to task over, as several of its big HD-2D RPGs have no upgrade path to Switch 2. For example, if you purchased Octopath Traveler for the Switch, there's no complimentary or premium upgrade pack to give it sharper graphics and new features on a Switch 2 console. Instead, you'll have to buy the game again when its Switch 2 version launches, and you don't even get an option to transfer your save game over. All of this paints a worrying picture for game…

title: This Fake CRT TV Is A Brilliant Idea That Fails In The Most Essential Way
description: If you ask any retro nerd enthusiast like me what's the best way to experience classic gaming consoles, they're always going to start yapping at you about CRTs. And for good reason: CRTs offer zero input latency, variable refresh rate, and the best picture quality for viewing classic games. Many games designed their art around the visual intricacies of these old tube TVs to create transparent effects or blend colors to create detail not present when viewed as sharp pixels. CRT Pixels makes excellent comparisons showing how pixel art is supposed to look when viewed on a CRT. But CRTs in 2026 come with a lot of problems. They are hard to find and can often be expensive or not in ideal condition. CRTs are also not commercially made anymore (outside of very rare and expensive niches), meaning we now live in a world with a finite supply of them. One day we're going to run out, and we're going to need a solution. Digital shaders have gotten really good as of late, applying post-effects that recreate scanlines, color, and even recreating image-bending around the corners on non-CRT displays. But these exist in the world of emulators and retro scaling devices. I’ve always wanted to see this taken one step further with a display built from the ground up and designed for retro consoles, something that can accept old input standards and can offer excellent post-effect features that help simulate a CRT. A Retrotink-Monitor if you will. That is initially what got me excited about the Traveller ULW10 from Unico. This is a portable display housed in a shell that's designed to look like the classic Sony PVM. To be clear, this is not a CRT. This is an LCD monitor wrapped in cute nostalgic retro packaging. Unico itself is known for creating LCD replacements for arcade cabinets. The Traveller ULW10 models itself after a Sony PVM I'm under no illusion that this thing would be a 1-to-1 replacement for a CRT. But if it can get close, this could be exactly what I’ve been wanting: a nice…

title: Ocarina Of Time Remake’s Map And Level Design Looks Quite Similar To The Original So Far
description: Nintendo's Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct has given us the first gameplay deep dive, showing how the 1998 N64 classic has been updated for Nintendo Switch 2, from a new detailed art style to new control additions like a jump button and motion-control aiming. However, from this first look, it also looks like the game will be sticking closely, if not identically, to the original game's layout. The environments shown in the starting Kokiri Forest area are a lot more detailed, and you can now see them from a new perspective thanks to a free rotating camera. However, you can also see that the minimap the bottom-right of the screen shows the layout of the area is almost identical to the original game. Glimpses of the first dungeon, Inside The Great Deku Tree, also have a similar layout. There are nonetheless some modern touches, such as how when Link reaches the chest containing the slingshot, he has to across a wooden path that collapses whereas in the original this was a floating collapsing platform. The surest sign came from our first look of Hyrule Field, which has been the topic of speculation over whether this iconic location would be expanded to a size that would reflect the scale of a modern open environment. From the panning of the camera showing familiar landmarks like Death Mountain and Hyrule Castle Town, it looks like the size and scale of the world is staying very close to the original, including how you still load in between areas rather than traverse a whole seamless Hyrule. Nonetheless, the minimap of Hyrule Field does appear wider and so it doesn't rule out the possibility of new activities and side quests. Link can also now sprint across the map and jump at any time, which may also open up new options. Although Ocarina of Time may not be hugely expanding the original on a similar scale as Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, it's also reflected in its $60 price point for the digital version of the game, which is still less than the full price of new releases--the…

title: After Decades Of Making Us Play As Men, GTA 6’s Lucia Has A Lot To Prove
description: Grand Theft Auto has always had a complicated relationship with women. For decades, it’s been known as the series where you can visit a strip club, hire a sex worker, and swiftly beat her to death in the nearest alley. Violence against women in virtual settings praised for their unflinching realism is frequently turned into a punchline players are expected to chuckle at again and again and again. With the series achieving mainstream global stardom at a time when the medium was still predominantly an archaic boy’s club, it’s no surprise it has stuck around. But with the arrival of player character Lucia Caminos in the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6 later this year, Rockstar has an opportunity to completely redefine the franchise’s problematic dynamic with women and potentially introduce one of the strongest female protagonists this medium has ever seen--but we all know that sticking the landing is easier said than done. People often claim that everybody is an equal target in GTA’s vast and satiristic worlds, but it’s hard to understand that perspective when all the protagonists are men and most female characters around them are used to advance their stories, rather than be a substantial part of them. Past GTA women typically haven't had genuine agency or personalities that aren’t compounded by misogynistic cliche. There are rare bright sparks, such as hardened crime lord Asuka Kasen in GTA 3 or San Andrea’s emotionally intelligent Kendl Johnson. But it’s difficult not to turn my nose up at the erratic white privilege of Michael De Santa’s wife and daughter, Franklin’s Aunt Denise and her obsession with upending the patriarchy, or GTA 3’s Catalina, who after betraying Claude at the end of the game is killed in what amounts to an off-screen gag. These are jokes and storytelling that have aged poorly, especially now that Rockstar has proven it can write mature and nuanced female characters like Sadie Adler in Red Dead Redemption 2. That game was a masterpiece…

title: Here’s How Jace Tokens Work In Magic: The Gathering’s Reality Fracture Expansion
description: Magic: The Gathering's final in-universe expansion of the year, Reality Fracture, is a consequential one for the lore of MTG. The current story arc, in which longtime hero Jace Beleren has become the overarching villain, reaches its conclusion here, and with Jace playing such a pivotal role in the story, it makes sense that he also plays a major part in the cards. In fact, Jace is the focus of a new mechanic debuting in Reality Fracture, one that lead designer Mark Rosewater has been hyping up since MagicCon Atlanta in September 2025. That mechanic, as announced today during the Reality Fracture reveal stream, is the Jace Token, a new type of token that focuses on Planeswalker abilities. Here's how the token works. Empowering Jace Throughout Reality Fracture, there are cards with the keywords "Empower Jace," followed by a number. Protege's Awakening, for example, is a four-mana sorcery spell that reads "Empower Jace 6." Whenever you play a card or activate an ability with Empower Jace, you will add loyalty counters to a Jace Token equal to the number next to the keyword; for Protege's Awakening, for example, you'll add six counters. If you don't already have a Jace token, you'll add one to the board, and then place the counters on it. The Jace token, meanwhile, is a Planeswalker with two abilities: You can either remove one loyalty counter to surveil 1--or look at the top card of your library and either return it to the top of your library or put it in the graveyard--or you can remove three loyalty counters to draw a card. An intriguing technicality While this all makes sense within the confines of Reality Fracture, what about in the broader Magic landscape? Jace fans are going to like this answer: If you're able to make a copy of another Jace planeswalker card, and you use an Empower Jace ability, you can elect to put the counters onto the copied Jace rather than the Jace token itself. For example, if you were to activate the second ability of Tamiyo, Compleated…

title: GameStop Sets A New Financial Record, And It’s No Thanks To Games
description: Retailer GameStop has released its latest earnings report, and it was a record-breaker for the company. The Texas-based retailer's biggest number for its fiscal Q2 quarter that ended August 1 was $160.2 million. That's how much GameStop made in operating income for the period, and it was the highest Q2 operating income level since the company went public in 2002. Net income was up, too, reaching $298.7 million, compared to $168.6 million last year. GameStop benefitted from continued growth in its biggest sales category--collectibles--which saw net sales jump a whopping 57% year-over-year to $356.3 million. For this latest period, collectibles made up 45.1% of GameStop's net sales. GameStop was once primarily known as a video game retailer, and while it still sells games, consoles, and accessories, the company's biggest revenue-driver today is collectibles. Anyone who has walked into a GameStop store recently can attest to how much shelf space is dedicated to collectibles. GameStop's next-largest revenue-driver was its "video game" category, which reached $263.2 million for the period, down sharply from $494.6 million during the same period last year that benefitted from the Switch 2 launch. Finally, GameStop's pre-owned and refurbished business made up $170.7 million during the period, down from $250 million last year. Some might have thought that Sony's decision to end support for physical game discs, and GTA 6 not releasing on a disc, would be a death knell for a company like GameStop. However, physical video game sales are "irrelevant" to the company, CEO Ryan Cohen has said. He has also suggested GameStop could expand its business into the "live commerce" category that is popular on TikTok. title: NBA 2K27 gives DLSS 5 a more faithful-looking game debut than feared, provided it’s running on the LeBron of GPUs
description: Bit of an anticlimax, really. After months of (justified) revulsion and anti-anticipation over Nvidia DLSS 5 ’s AI rendering, it’s now available in a live game - license laden b-baller NBA 2K27 - and it looks... maybe not that bad? This not-that-badness does come at an enormous cost to performance, and I’m still sceptical of how DLSS 5 will handle something more stylised than 2K27’s devotedly realistic depictions of varnished court floors and face-scanned athletes. But given how artistically botching and/or ridden with rendering errors the earlier previews have been, this specific implementation, in this specific game, is at least inoffensive in the looks department.
